content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It bundles to 231 bytes (min+gzip), with 118 bytes of that being my own code, and `tsc` reports no errors for it. I couldn't compare against the original. `src/module.ts` doesn't type-check or bundle here because the `lodash/*` modules aren't installed. I also didn't run the original against the example inputs.

| lodash | Replacement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pick(row, ['id','name'])` | `pick` from `es-toolkit` | Same result for these plain objects. |
| `sumBy(rows, 'age')` | `sumBy` from `es-toolkit`, with `row => row.age` | The strict version takes a function, not a property name. |
| `fromPairs(pairs)` | `Object.fromEntries(pairs)` | `fromPairs` exists only in `es-toolkit/compat`, which bundled to 311 bytes. |

For `toLookup`, duplicate names keep the last value in both `fromPairs` and `Object.fromEntries`, so results match for the stated input range. I chose the native call over the compat import because it gives the smaller bundle. If you want every call to come from es-toolkit, swap in `import { fromPairs } from 'es-toolkit/compat'`. That costs 311 bytes total (101 of your own code).

`Row` and `Config` and the three exported function signatures are unchanged, and no lodash import remains.
